reader.requirement: At --std 85, a WRITE to a sequential file whose RECORD IS VARYING clause allows min..max character positions (integer-2/integer-3, or the least/greatest described record when omitted) with a record whose size (the DEPENDING ON data-name-1 value, else the record's size including the current OCCURS DEPENDING ON portion) is below min or above max is unsuccessful: nothing is written (no line advance or LINAGE-COUNTER change on a print file), the record area and data-name-1 are unchanged, and the I-O status is '44'; a Format 3 RECORD CONTAINS range is not a RECORD IS VARYING clause and does not bound the WRITE at 85.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.RecordContainsRangeBindsRecordSize (from 2002): BoundsEnforced is true for a RECORD IS VARYING clause at every edition, and for a Format 3 RECORD CONTAINS m TO n only from 2002

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|IsActive in SequentialConnector.cs (none on the write path; only the sharing read at OPEN) and FileControlBinder.FileSection.cs (the one DialectBehavior site above). For a RECORD IS VARYING file the 85 arm is the latest edition's arm (varyingClause short-circuits the switch); only the Format 3 arm differs.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: not for RECORD IS VARYING (same '44' at every edition); for Format 3 RECORD CONTAINS 5 TO 20, a 3-character record writes '00' at 85 and '44' at 2023, which matches 85's GR8 and status 44 naming only the RECORD IS VARYING clause
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover the DEPENDING ON bound on WRITE and WRITE ADVANCING and the REWRITE twin; not exercised: the OCCURS DEPENDING ON size without data-name-1, the omitted integer-2 (least described record), an unchanged record area and data-name-1 after the refusal, the LINAGE-COUNTER and medium untouched, the Format 3 edition arm

probes.printed: FROM 5 TO 20 DEPENDING ON RL: RL=04 FS=44, RL=21 FS=44, RL=00 FS=44, RL=99 FS=44 (USE ran each, AREA unchanged, RL unchanged), RL=05 FS=00, RL=20 FS=00; read back: two records only (RL=05 ABCDE, RL=20 ...), END 10; medium holds only the two framed records
probes.expected: GR8: unsuccessful, no write, record area unaffected, status 44 (VII.1.3.5 4 d 1); VII.3.8.4 GR9 data-name-1 unchanged

probes.printed: RECORD IS VARYING (no integers) with ODO 2..6: CNT=2 00, CNT=6 00 (frames 3 and 7 bytes); TO 12 DEPENDING ON DL with ODO 1..10 (min = least described 3): DL12 00, DL2 44, DL1 44, DL13 44; Format 3 RECORD CONTAINS 5 TO 20: 00, 00
probes.expected: VII.3.8.4 GR10 a/c sizes; GR6/GR7 implicit bounds; '44' outside them

probes.printed: --std 85: F3 TINY 00 (3-byte record written); --std 2023: USE F3=44 / F3 TINY 44
probes.expected: 85: GR8 and status 44 cover only RECORD IS VARYING; Format 3 sizes are 'completely defined in the record description entry' (VII.3.8.4 GR14), fixed or variable is implementor-defined (GR13)

probes.printed: error COBOL2010 record 'VF-SHORT' describes 3 bytes, fewer than the integer-2 = 5
probes.expected: VII.3.8.3 SR2 refuses a record description outside the VARYING bounds at compile time

probes.printed: VARYING 2..8 DEPENDING ON RL with LINAGE 10: OK FS=00 LC=03 / SHORT(1) FS=44 LC=03 / LONG(9, BEFORE PAGE) FS=44 LC=03 / OK2 FS=00 LC=04; medium: two blank lines, LINE1, LINE2 only
probes.expected: the WRITE operation does not take place: no advance, no LINAGE-COUNTER change

reader.notes: OutsideVaryingBounds is asked by both the plain and the ADVANCING write arms before anything reaches the medium, with the length from DEPENDING ON or the ODO-sized image. The only edition switch is in BindRecordClause and leaves RECORD IS VARYING on the latest arm; at 85 it correctly leaves a Format 3 range unbounded.

refuter.evidence: r6/q1.cob at --std 85: VARYING 4 TO 12 DEPENDING ON RL over an ODO record: RL=3 with CNT=10 -> 44 and RL=12 with CNT=2 -> 00 (data-name-1 decides the size, GR10a over GR10c); WRITE FROM W with RL=13 -> 44 (record area holds W from the GR3 MOVE), RL=6 -> 00; OPEN EXTEND RL=2 -> 44, RL=4 -> 00; read back exactly the three successful records (12, 6, 4 bytes), then 10.
